Let \( a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots \) be the unique sequence of nonnegative integers less than 397 with \( a_0 = 1 \) and

\[ a_{n+1}(a_n + 1)^2 \equiv a_n \pmod{397} \]

for all nonnegative integers \( n \). Given that \( a_{2026} = 9 \), compute the remainder when \( a_0 + a_1 + \cdots + a_{2026} \) is divided by 397.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Work modulo \(397\), which is prime, so nonzero residues have inverses.

The needed terms are nonzero: since \(a_{2026}=9\), none of \(a_0,\dots,a_{2026}\) can be \(0\), and \(a_{2027}\neq 0\) follows from the recurrence.

From
\[
a_{n+1}(a_n+1)^2\equiv a_n \pmod{397},
\]
we get
\[
\frac1{a_{n+1}}\equiv \frac{(a_n+1)^2}{a_n}.
\]
Thus
\[
\frac1{a_{n+1}}-\frac1{a_n}
\equiv \frac{(a_n+1)^2-1}{a_n}
= a_n+2.
\]
So
\[
a_n\equiv \frac1{a_{n+1}}-\frac1{a_n}-2.
\]

Summing from \(n=0\) to \(2026\),
\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv \left(\frac1{a_{2027}}-\frac1{a_0}\right)-2(2027).
\]
Since \(a_0=1\),
\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv \frac1{a_{2027}}-1-4054.
\]

Now \(a_{2026}=9\), so
\[
a_{2027}\cdot 10^2\equiv 9 \pmod{397}.
\]
Hence
\[
\frac1{a_{2027}}\equiv \frac{100}{9}\pmod{397}.
\]
Since \(9^{-1}\equiv 353 \pmod{397}\),
\[
\frac{100}{9}\equiv 100\cdot 353\equiv 364 \pmod{397}.
\]
Also,
\[
4054\equiv 84 \pmod{397}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv 364-1-84
=279 \pmod{397}.
\]

\[
\boxed{279}
\]
